title: Binary Market Data Decoder

statement.md: A feed handler receives binary packets, given here as hex strings (two hex digits per byte, upper or lower case). All integers are big endian. Every packet starts with a 4 byte sequence number and a 1 byte type:
Expected sequence starts at 1. Process packets in order:

items: A packet with fewer than 5 bytes (or an odd number of hex digits) prints `ERR LENGTH -` and does not touch the sequence state.
If $\text{seq} < \text{expected}$, print `DUP seq` and ignore the packet completely.

If $\text{seq} > \text{expected}$, print `GAP expected seq-1` (the missing range, inclusive) and continue with this packet. After this check, set expected to $\text{seq}+1$, even if the packet turns out to be invalid.
Unknown type byte, or an `A` with a side other than `B`/`S`: print `ERR TYPE seq`. Wrong total length for the type: print `ERR LENGTH seq`.
`A` adds a live order with that id and quantity; if the id is already live print `ERR DUPID seq` and change nothing.

`X` and `E` reduce the live quantity of the order. Unknown id: print `ERR UNKNOWN seq`. Quantity larger than the remaining quantity: print `ERR OVERFLOW seq` and change nothing. An order whose remaining quantity reaches 0 is removed. `E` also adds its quantity to the executed total.

statement.md: A valid packet prints nothing. After all packets print `BOOK n` (number of live orders) and `SHARES m` (executed total). Ids are compared as 64-bit numbers, so upper and lower case hex are the same id.

inputFormat: First line: $n$. Then $n$ lines, each a hex string.
outputFormat: Event lines in packet order, then `BOOK n` and `SHARES m`.
constraints: Each line has at most 64 hex digits
Quantities of valid `A`, `X`, `E` packets are at least 1

examples.output:
GAP 3 3
DUP 3
ERR UNKNOWN 5
BOOK 0
SHARES 40

hints: Decode bytes by hand: two hex digits per byte, then fold big endian into an integer.
Check the sequence number first, then the type, then the length, then the order book.

editorial.md: The order of checks defines the output. Sequence handling comes first and is applied even to invalid packets; then the type and length are checked; only a fully valid packet touches the book.
Use 64-bit integers for the executed total and keep ids as 64-bit values or normalised lower case strings.
